biography.plain_text: Luigi Frati was an Italian industrialist who built a wood-panel manufacturing group in Pomponesco. He began as a haulier before establishing his first factory in the early 1960s. The business moved from plywood into chipboard and expanded into Friuli through Bipan. His daughter Giovanna subsequently took over the group's management.

long_biography.plain_text:
Luigi Frati approached investment in machinery as a way to make his panel factories more adaptable. At Pomponesco, a continuous press allowed several changes of product size and thickness during a single day. When choosing new equipment for Bicinicco, he sought similar flexibility in producing fibreboard at different densities.

Installing the new line inside an existing building required the roof to be removed so heavy components could be lowered into place. Frati credited the work of his engineering subsidiary's technical managers. His aim was to improve efficiency and quality within the existing business, serving Italian furniture makers rather than simply increasing output.
